item.title: Japan’s 30-Year Bond Sale Demand Stronger Than 12-Month Average
item.description: Japan’s 30-year government bond auction Thursday saw stronger demand than the 12-month average as elevated yields underpinned buying.

item.title: India’s Rupee Gains as RBI Measures Bring in Bumper $136 Billion
item.description: India’s rupee gained as the central bank garnered $136 billion under its capital-raising measures, far exceeding expectations and further boosting its war chest to defend the currency.

item.title: HDFC Bank Is at Risk of Losing Its Top Nifty Spot to Rival ICICI
item.description: HDFC Bank Ltd. is barely holding on to its position as the most influential stock on India’s equity benchmark as a leadership upheaval and governance concerns deepen a selloff.

item.title: Base Metals Gain Ground as Trump Says Iran Attacks Will Be Brief
item.description: Metals advanced after President Donald Trump said that a new wave of US attacks on Iran would likely be short-lived, easing concerns about further escalation in the region that hurt prices on Wednesday.

item.title: Yen Traders Brace for Holiday Intervention Risk Around BOJ
item.description: Yen traders are on heightened alert for possible intervention around the Bank of Japan’s upcoming policy meeting, with a three-day holiday following the decision offering authorities an opportunity to act in thinner trading.

item.title: HDFC Bank’s Nifty Crown Under Threat From ICICI Bank After CEO Exit
item.description: Lender’s shares have tumbled 29% this year, their worst showing relative to the Nifty Bank gauge since 2003.

item.title: Singapore Ruling on Bankrupt Indonesian Firm May Open Recovery Path for Others
item.description: A Singapore court’s landmark decision allowing administrators of bankrupt Indonesian textile maker PT Sri Rejeki Isman to pursue assets in the city-state may open a new route to recoveries for investors in other insolvent Indonesian firms with links to Singapore.

item.title: ByteDance Gets $30 Billion Loan, Asia’s Second-Largest This Year
item.description: ByteDance Ltd., the developer of TikTok, has secured a $29.6 billion loan, according to people familiar with the matter, in Asia’s second-largest dollar-denominated borrowing this year.

item.title: Vietnam Trade Gap Narrows to $113 Million; Inflation Faster
item.description: Vietnam’s trade deficit drastically narrowed in August as the government pushes to reduce the nation’s reliance on imported components for its booming manufacturing sector.

item.title: Fitch Sees Thai Risks Easing Ahead of Rating Review, Citing Political Stability
item.description: Thailand is heading into Fitch Ratings’ annual review with risks receding from a year ago, when political uncertainty and mounting debt prompted a negative outlook on its credit.

item.title: China’s Services Gauge Tops Forecasts With Surprise Rebound
item.description: China’s services activity expanded far more than forecast in August, a private survey showed, contrasting with signs of weak demand across the world’s second-biggest economy.

item.title: Japan Trading House Stocks Gain as Berkshire Signals Support
item.description: Shares of Japanese trading houses rose after Berkshire Hathaway Inc.’s Chief Executive Officer Greg Abel signaled long-term commitment to the firms, and that it may invest more.

item.title: Hongkong Land Eyes Billion-Dollar Property Deals to Enter Japan
item.description: One of Hong Kong’s biggest landlords is in talks to enter Japan’s resurgent property market as part of parent Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd.’s pivot toward becoming an investment firm, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Korean FX Reserves Swell by Record $14.3 Billion in August
item.description: South Korea’s foreign-exchange reserves rose by a record $14.33 billion in August, driven by a jump in commercial banks’ foreign-currency deposits at the central bank.

item.title: Diversified Energy Buys Elliott-Backed Birch for $1.8 Billion
item.description: Diversified Energy Co. agreed to acquire Elliott Investment Management-backed oil and gas company Birch Resources in a deal valued at about $1.8 billion.

item.title: Pakistan Raises $3 Billion in Two-Part Junk Bond Sale
item.description: Pakistan raised $3 billion from a two-part junk bond sale, taking advantage of investor interest after securing credit rating upgrades in the past couple of months.

item.title: Malaysia Set to Hold Rates as Investors Bet on Tightening Ahead
item.description: Malaysia’s central bank is expected to keep interest rates unchanged on Thursday, with subdued inflation giving policymakers little reason to tighten despite resilient economic growth.

item.title: Gold Rises Above $4,400 as Trump Comments Ease Inflation Concern
item.description: Gold rose for a second day as US President Donald Trump appeared to rule out prolonged military action in the Middle East, easing inflationary concerns driven by a renewed spike in energy prices.

item.title: Japan’s 30-Year Bond Auction Risks Adding Fuel to Debt Selloff
item.description: Japan’s 30-year government bond auction Thursday will test investor appetite as a global selloff pushes long-dated yields to their highest levels in almost two decades.

item.title: Chevron CEO Says Patience Pays Off in Venezuela Oil Deal
item.description: Big Oil has often employed the “hang around” playbook: secure legal rights to a giant resource — and then, eventually, figure out how to produce it profitably. But few companies have taken it to the extremes of Chevron Corp.

item.title: Uber, Wayve Launch Robotaxi Service in London to Compete With Waymo
item.description: The centuries-old roads in the UK capital present challenges that Los Angeles and San Francisco don’t.

item.title: Asia Dollar Gauge’s Surge Masks Two-Tier Currency Market
item.description: Asia’s currency gauge has been on a two-month tear, with one measure of its relationship to the dollar close to a record low. But its strength belies a two-tier divide, with currencies of technology-heavy exporters roaring ahead and set to further outperform peers less cushioned against high oil prices.

item.title: ASML Supplier Says China 15 Years Behind in Top Chipmaking Tools
item.description: China is about a decade and a half behind in developing cutting-edge chipmaking tools, according to a top executive at Germany’s Zeiss Group, a key supplier in the global semiconductor industry.

item.title: Five Below Lifts Outlook, Aims to Ramp Up Appeal to Gen Alpha
item.description: Five Below Inc. shares rose over 8% in postmarket trading on Wednesday after the retailer lifted its full-year outlook, citing the addition of new stores and the popularity of its budget-friendly merchandise among Gen Alpha and Gen Z shoppers.

item.title: TikTok Backs Out of House Meeting to Avoid Kids Safety Questions
item.description: TikTok dropped out of an upcoming meeting with the House Select Committee on China on national security issues, saying it couldn’t participate because of unrelated child-safety litigation, the leader of the panel said.

item.title: Petco Services, Auto-Ship Sales Grow as Turnaround Continues
item.description: Petco Health & Wellness Co. shares rose as much as 14% in postmarket trading Wednesday after the pet supply retailer reported profit above Wall Street expectations and comparable sales grew for the second straight quarter after a year of declines.

item.title: Asian Stocks Set to Advance as Oil Pressures Ease: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were poised to track Wall Street higher as oil’s surge eased after President Donald Trump played down the prospect of a prolonged conflict with Iran, tempering inflation concerns.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 3
item.description: Oil steadied after a three-day rally as President Donald Trump said renewed attacks on Iran would be short-lived while reiterating his claim that the US controls the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Australian Earnings Beat Estimates for First Time in Four Years
item.description: Australian earnings beats are outpacing misses for the first time in four years, defying a challenging economic backdrop and bolstering chances for a stalled stock rally to resume.

item.title: Japanese Companies Consider Asset Sales as Yen Debt Costs Rise
item.description: Japanese companies are expanding their toolkit to deal with the steepest borrowing costs in a generation, including considering sales of strategic shareholdings and other assets to offset the impact, a Bloomberg News survey shows.
